newsitem.title: ROMANIA: ROMANIA BRM CALLS TENDER FOR SOVIET-MADE AIRCRAFT.
newsitem.headline: ROMANIA BRM CALLS TENDER FOR SOVIET-MADE AIRCRAFT.

text.p: Romania's Bucharest-based commodities exchange will call a tender to sell two-Soviet made aircraft owned by the state airline Tarom SA this month, the exchange said on Tuesday.
The offer include two Ilyushin Il-62M aircraft as well as spare parts, Bursa Romana de Marfuri (BRM) said in a statement.

The minimum starting price for the Il-62M marked YR-IRD is $300,000, while for the second aircraft identified as YR-IRE is $500,000, the statement said. Bidders have until August 22 to submit offers for the tender. Starting price for the spare parts is $150,000, it said.
BRM gave no details related to the technical condition of the two aircraft offered in the tender scheduled for August 25.
The two aircraft come from a batch of about 20 Soviet-made planes which Tarom plans to sell through the BRM as part of its moves to restructure the airline.

Tarom's Soviet-era fleet includes 14 Antonov-24s, four Ilyushin Il-18s and seven Tupolev Tu-154Bs, company soUrces said recently. The planes are in "good shape" and have long hours of service ahead, the sources also said.
